name: StillAnotherSite
author: studionamaste

sections.description:
StillAnotherSite is a free Elementor template library with 3,000+ ready-to-use design blocks and page sections. Browse over 30 categories of professionally designed templates — hero sections, call-to-action blocks, testimonials, pricing tables, footers, and more — preview thumbnails, and import any block into your Elementor page with a single click. No coding required.

Whether you are building a landing page, a sales page, a business website, or a portfolio, StillAnotherSite gives you pre-designed sections that you can drag, drop, and customize. Skip the blank canvas and start with high-end layouts.

Key features:

  • 100+ free blocks — available immediately, no license or account required. Start building right away.
  • 3,000+ premium blocks via the template service — connect your license key to access the full library of Elementor design blocks and starter templates.
  • One-click import — each block is inserted directly into your current Elementor page as a new section. Pick, insert, done.
  • 30+ categories — hero, navbar, footer, FAQ, testimonials, call-to-action, pricing, gallery, team, features, counters, contact, blog grid, and more.
  • PRO badge — blocks that require Elementor Pro widgets are clearly marked so you know what you need before importing.
  • Landing pages & sales pages — combine hero, features, testimonials, and CTA blocks to build high-converting pages in minutes.
  • License management — activate and deactivate your license from the WordPress Settings page (Settings → StillAnotherSite).

External services

This plugin connects to an external service hosted at stillanothersite.studionamaste.net, which is operated by the plugin author (Studio Namaste). The service provides the template library and license management.

Template library

When browsing or importing templates inside the Elementor editor, the plugin fetches template data (JSON, images, ZIP archives) from the service API. The service determines which templates are available based on the user’s authentication status.

Data sent: an access token (issued after license validation) and the requested template/category identifiers.
This happens every time the user opens the template library or imports a block.

License activation and validation

When a user activates, validates, or deactivates a license key, the plugin sends the license key and the site URL to the service API. The license key is used to authenticate with the template service.
This also happens automatically in the background to refresh the license status, and on plugin uninstall to release the license.

Service: https://stillanothersite.studionamaste.net
Terms of use: https://stillanothersite.studionamaste.net/terms-of-use/
Privacy policy: https://stillanothersite.studionamaste.net/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • PHP 8.1 or higher
  • Elementor (free version) installed and active

Steps

  1. Install and activate Elementor if you have not already.
  2. Upload the stillanothersite folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the plugin through the WordPress plugin screen.
  3. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  4. Open any page or post with the Elementor editor.
  5. Look for the SAS button in the Elementor editor toolbar. Click it to open the StillAnotherSite template library.

How to use (no license needed)

  1. Open the Elementor editor on any page.
  2. Click the SAS button to open the template library popup.
  3. Select a category from the dropdown, browse the thumbnails, and click Insert on any block to add it to your page.
  4. That is it — no license key, no account, no configuration required.

How to access more blocks (license key)

  1. Purchase a license at stillanothersite.studionamaste.net. You will receive a license key via email.
  2. In WordPress, go to Settings → StillAnotherSite.
  3. Enter your license key and click Activate License.
  4. Open the Elementor editor and click the SAS button. The template service now provides additional blocks in each category.

How to deactivate a license

  1. In WordPress, go to Settings → StillAnotherSite.
  2. Click Deactivate License. The license is released from this site and you can reuse the key on a different site.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin require Elementor?

Yes. Elementor (free version or Pro) must be installed and active. The plugin adds its template library button inside the Elementor editor interface.

Where is the SAS button?

When editing a page with Elementor, look for a small SAS icon button at the bottom-left of the editor panel. Clicking it opens the template library popup.

Can I use the plugin without a license key?

Yes. Without a license key, the template service provides 100+ design blocks that you can browse, preview, and import freely. No registration required.

How do I get a license key for more blocks?

Visit stillanothersite.studionamaste.net and purchase a plan. You will receive a license key via email after purchase. With a license, the template service provides access to additional blocks.

Where do I enter my license key?

Go to Settings → StillAnotherSite in the WordPress admin. Enter your key and click Activate License.

Can I use my license key on multiple sites?

Each license key is linked to a single site. To use it on a different site, first deactivate it from the current site via Settings → StillAnotherSite, then activate it on the new site.

What happens when I import a block?

The block is added as a new Elementor section at the end of your current page. You can then move, edit, or restyle it like any other Elementor section.

What are PRO badges on some blocks?

Blocks marked with a PRO badge use Elementor Pro widgets (such as Loop Grid, Posts, or other Pro-only elements). You need Elementor Pro installed to use these blocks fully. They can still be imported with the free version of Elementor, but Pro widgets will not render correctly without Elementor Pro.

Can I build a landing page or sales page with this plugin?

Yes. Combine hero sections, feature blocks, testimonials, call-to-action buttons, pricing tables, and footer sections to assemble a complete landing page or sales page in minutes. Each block is a ready-to-use Elementor section that you can customize after importing.

What categories of blocks are available?

The library includes 30+ categories: hero, hero slider, navbar, footer, call-to-action, features, testimonials, pricing table, FAQ, contact, gallery, blog grid, team grid, counters, content, video, list, icon box, image box, portfolio, and more. New categories are added regularly.

Does the plugin work offline?

The template library requires a connection to the StillAnotherSite server to load block thumbnails and import templates. If the server is temporarily unavailable, the plugin uses a cached copy of the template index when available.
sections.changelog:
0.4

  • Removed client-side template access restrictions for WordPress.org compliance. Template availability is now determined entirely by the external template service.
  • Removed Free tab — all available blocks are shown in the Blocks tab.
  • Moved license management from the Elementor popup to a dedicated WordPress Settings page (Settings → StillAnotherSite).
  • After license activation or deactivation, the template service returns the updated set of blocks on the next editor session.
  • Cleaned up unused code (lock overlay, upgrade buttons, tier checking).

0.3

  • Fixed SAS button initialization race condition in the Elementor editor.
  • Populated bundled fallback index with real free templates for offline use.
  • Hidden category selector in Free tab for cleaner UX.
  • Improved readme with comprehensive usage instructions, FAQ, and external services documentation.

0.2

  • Refactored plugin into modular class architecture.
  • Added offline fallback system for template index.
  • Removed self-hosted updater for WordPress.org compliance.
  • Fixed option name prefixing for WordPress.org review.
  • Documented external service usage in readme.

0.1.5

  • Initial public release.
